# LongMemEval Corpus-Scale Sweep

**Status: pending run.** This file is a placeholder. It is regenerated by the
harness when the sweep is run; until then no numbers exist here.

## What the sweep measures

The access-recency retention window (per-doc_type: each `staleness_thresholds`
entry × `RETENTION_MULTIPLIER`, D3) trades recall for store size: evicting cold
docs shrinks the candidate pool, but evicting too aggressively drops docs a later
query needed. To gauge whether those windows are the right eviction points we need
to know how much *store bloat* actually crowds relevant docs out of
top-K — which only shows up on **real embeddings** (the FakeEmbedder ties every
vector at ~0.74 similarity, faking crowding; see design D8a).

The sweep (`--scale-sweep`) grows the corpus with irrelevant **distractor** docs
at increasing per-subcategory levels and re-scores the same gold slice at each
level, reporting R@K / MRR vs corpus size. Distractors are deterministic filler
(seeded by subcategory + index, drawn from a neutral vocabulary) so they never
semantically match a gold query — they only add pool depth. It is **not** a
go/no-go gate; it informs the default window.

## How to run

Real embeddings + the in-cluster bench instance (`memory-mcp-bench` on jx):

```sh
go run ./benchmarks/longmemeval \
  --data data/longmemeval_s_cleaned.json \
  --seed 42 --n 150 --k 5,10 --concurrency 16 \
  --scale-sweep 100,500,2000,10000
```

The base run is unchanged; the sweep runs after it and writes `results_scale.json`
+ this file. Each level N adds N distractors to every question's subcategory, so
the total corpus grows by N × (number of questions) per level.
